description: On courtesy, consideration and quiet dignity.

items.text: A gentleman is one who never hurts anyone's feelings unintentionally.
items.author: Attributed to Oscar Wilde

translations.en: A gentleman is one who never hurts anyone's feelings unintentionally.
translations.hi: सज्जन वह है जो कभी अनजाने में किसी की भावनाओं को ठेस न पहुँचाए।

items.summary_1line: Courtesy means care with others' feelings.
items.summary_2to3line: Refinement is measured by attentiveness, not display. The gentleman's default is to avoid causing needless hurt.
items.bodh_3to4line: Consideration is a practice, not a mood. It means noticing the effect of your words before you speak them, and treating the feelings of others as real. Small courtesies, consistently kept, are the whole thing.

items.author: Traditional proverb (William of Wykeham)

translations.hi: शिष्टाचार ही मनुष्य को मनुष्य बनाता है।

items.summary_2to3line: Behaviour and character are woven together. How you treat people is not a veneer - it is a large part of who you are.
items.bodh_3to4line: Good manners are the visible edge of inward respect. They cost nothing, ease everything, and quietly announce what kind of person you have decided to be.

items.text: Politeness is the flower of humanity.
items.author: Attributed to Joseph Joubert

translations.en: Politeness is the flower of humanity.

items.summary_1line: Politeness is a sign of our humanity.
items.summary_2to3line: Courtesy is a cultivated bloom, not a weakness. It shows that we can choose gentleness over impulse.
items.bodh_3to4line: Anyone can be kind when it is easy. Politeness shines when you are tired, rushed or annoyed. That is when it proves itself as a discipline rather than a mood.

items.text: The true gentleman is one whose conduct proceeds from good will and an acute sense of propriety.
items.author: Attributed to John Henry Newman

translations.en: The true gentleman is one whose conduct proceeds from good will and an acute sense of propriety.
translations.hi: सच्चा सज्जन वह है जिसका आचरण सद्भाव और औचित्य की सूक्ष्म समझ से निकलता है।

items.summary_1line: Good will, guided by good judgement.
items.summary_2to3line: It is not enough to mean well; the gentleman also reads the moment and acts fittingly.
items.bodh_3to4line: Kindness without judgement can wound; judgement without kindness can chill. The gentleman holds both: warmth of intent and a fine sense of what the situation actually calls for.

items.text: Kindness is a language which the deaf can hear and the blind can see.
items.author: Attributed to Mark Twain

translations.en: Kindness is a language which the deaf can hear and the blind can see.
translations.hi: दया एक ऐसी भाषा है जिसे बहरा सुन सकता है और अंधा देख सकता है।

items.summary_1line: Kindness needs no words to be felt.
items.summary_2to3line: Genuine kindness is perceived directly, beyond speech. It registers on anyone who receives it.
items.bodh_3to4line: You never fully know how much a small kindness matters to someone. Because it travels without words, it reaches people your cleverness never could. Give it freely.
